digest.component_or_area: code review criteria — tests and error-handling
propositions: A check whose PASS or definite result is indistinguishable from the check never having run produces a fail-open oracle defect, exemplified by absence assertions (not-in, assert-not, empty-grep) on subprocess/file/network output with no producer-liveness check.

The same broken instrument can produce a confident FAILING result for a reason other than the condition (e.g., zsh not word-splitting a multi-line variable), making the defect a mirror pattern: both pass and fail verdicts become untrustworthy.

Fail-open oracle language must be added to the existing tests criterion (test-oracle population) and error-handling criterion (shipped-code population), not as a new criterion, per operator ruling and calibration validation.

The remediation is uniform: assert the producer RAN (exit status, non-empty capture, liveness assertion) before trusting any absence derived from it, and the litmus is: name every world in which the check produces any definite result—if 'the producer never ran' or 'emitted nothing' is among them, the check cannot distinguish its verdict from its own failure.

Calibration corpus of nine seeded instances (five in error-handling host, four in tests host) must achieve 9/9 pre-fix recall (finding named the fail-open defect) and 9/9 post-fix silence (zero findings after liveness fix) to validate placement without a new criterion.
Documentation must appear in 'rebar explain review' (passing-code-review.md) with two worked examples (instances 1 and 6) since code-review criteria have no per-criterion explain surface.
